value.content: {"id": "portswigger_oauth", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "oauth", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: OAuth 2.0 & OpenID Connect", "name": "OAuth 2.0 Authentication & Token Flow Vulnerability Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-287", "owasp_category": "A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures", "signals": ["missing_state_parameter", "weak_redirect_uri_validation", "implicit_grant_token_leak", "authorization_code_reuse", "unverified_email_linking"], "verification_strategy": "Inspect OAuth authorization URLs for presence of the 'state' parameter. Test open redirection or domain bypasses on 'redirect_uri' (e.g. redirect_uri=https://example.com.attacker.com or path traversal). Test linking third-party OAuth accounts with pre-existing email accounts without verification.", "evidence_requirements": ["authorization_code_exfiltration", "state_parameter_omission_proof", "account_takeover_link_evidence"], "tools": [{"tool": "BrowserAgent (OAuth Flow)", "cmd": "BrowserAgent.audit_oauth_dance(url)", "desc": "Audits OAuth redirect_uri matching, state token presence, and authorization code lifecycle"}, {"tool": "BurpAgent (OAuth)", "cmd": "BurpAgent.replay_oauth_callback(code, state)", "desc": "Tests authorization code replay and cross-account code consumption"}], "remediation": "Enforce strict redirect_uri exact matching on the authorization server. Always require and cryptographically validate the state parameter to prevent CSRF in OAuth handshakes. Use PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange).", "description": "PortSwigger OAuth labs demonstrate stealing OAuth access tokens via open redirect in redirect_uri, OAuth CSRF through state parameter omission, and account hijacking via unverified email address linking."}
